summary: Koshko et al. report selected benzene-versus-filtered-air gene directions in P21 male hypothalamus. The paper identifies individual offspring libraries and describes separate analyses by sex, but leaves litter handling unspecified. None of the author results reviewed can be attributed to an exposure effect estimated across independent litters as in the registered contrast.

manualReview.summary: The paper reports P21 male gene directions. Its methods do not establish the litter-level comparison used by HypoExplorer.
manualReview.note: GEO records nine filtered-air and seven exposed male libraries after Xist-based sex reassignment. Excluding GSM7163652 (OBFH14), as the paper specifies, leaves nine and six. Section 2.4 describes reverse-strand STAR counts, removal of transcripts with fewer than 20 total reads, DESeq2 with apeglm shrinkage separately by sex, and a BH-adjusted P cutoff of 0.1 (strictly less than). The authors report 66 male DEGs. Figure 1B shows group-average expression for selected genes across four sex-by-exposure groups, including higher Ucp2 and lower Ebf2 in exposed males. The figure gives neither numerical exposure coefficients nor gene-level P or FDR values. The RNA-seq methods give no design formula, litter term or aggregation step. The registered edgeR quasi-likelihood model uses reverse-strand count sums within each of three litters per arm and estimates prenatal benzene relative to filtered air. The publisher DOCX and preprint PDF contain CX30 imaging and body-composition figures. All 33 declared GEO sample files contain STAR counts. No author gene-level result reviewed establishes a compatible litter-level effect.
reviewFlags: Sibling libraries came from the same exposure-assigned dams. The published methods leave their dependence in the DE model unresolved. Effect concordance and gene-level inference for the registered six-litter comparison remain unassessed.

verificationReview.reason: The tissue, P21 time point, male stratum and exposure direction agree. The author panel and narrative identify selected gene directions, but neither gives the six litter profiles or documents a model accounting for siblings within dams. A gene-level benchmark for the registered litter effect could not be established.
verificationReview.nextStep: Reopen if author code, a design and sample mapping, or gene-level results establish that the reported effects estimate the same male P21 benzene-versus-air effect with litters as the independent exposure units. Within-litter sums or a justified compatible analysis could establish this. Verify gene identifiers and effect definitions, limit any comparison to the available genes, and assess P/FDR only where supplied.
